Over 7 years at Extern, he has had one-on-one sessions with thousands of students exploring careers in consulting, finance, tech, marketing, and data, giving him a firsthand view of how the job market has shifted for early-career professionals and what it actually takes to break in.

title: How Many Hours Is Part-Time? An Employer's Guide
summary: There's no federal definition of part-time, which leaves the policy call to you as the employer. This guide walks through the federal stack (FLSA, ACA), state-specific rules, how to set your own policy, and what part-time vs full-time classification means for benefits, overtime, and 401(k) eligibility.
body_text: If you're creating or revising a part-time and full-time policy, one question probably comes up first: How many hours is considered part-time? The answer is less straightforward than many employers expect. Federal law does not establish a universal definition of part-time employment, which means employers often have flexibility when setting their own policies. However, laws such as the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), the Affordable Care Act (ACA), state and local employment laws, and benefits and retirement plan requirements can all influence how you define and manage part-time employees, including establishing hours-worked thresholds. As employers making these decisions, understanding the broader types of employment can provide helpful context for how part-time and full-time positions fit within an overall workforce strategy. This guide explains what may count as part-time and full-time employment, the federal and state rules to consider, and the practical steps employers can take when developing workforce policies. How Many Hours Is Part-Time? The Short Answer There is no federal definition of part-time employment. Instead, employers generally establish their own part-time and full-time definitions. In practice, many organizations define part-time employment as fewer than 30, 35, or 40 hours per week, depending on their business needs and benefit programs. Several common benchmarks influence these decisions: The Affordable Care Act (ACA) generally considers employees who average 30 or more hours per week to be full-time for employer group medical coverage purposes. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) often uses 35 hours per week as a statistical benchmark for full-time employment. Many employers use internal policies that define full-time status somewhere between 30 and 40 hours per week. As a result, an employee working 25 hours per week may be considered part-time at one organization and full-time at another, depending on the employer's policies and applicable compliance requirements. What Counts as Full-Time? Like part-time employment, there is no single federal definition of full-time employment that applies in every circumstance. Different laws and agencies, like the ACA and BLS, use different standards, as referenced above. For employees with fluctuating schedules, also referred to as variable hours, employers may need to apply measurement and tracking methods to determine whether an individual qualifies as full-time under applicable regulations. The Federal Framework: FLSA, ACA, and What They Require Understanding part-time versus full-time starts with understanding the major federal laws that affect workforce management. FLSA: Overtime, Minimum Wage, and the 40-Hour Week The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) establishes federal minimum wage and overtime requirements. However, it does not define part-time or full-time employment. What the FLSA does require is that non-exempt employees generally receive overtime pay when they work more than 40 hours in a workweek. Defining as part-time does not exempt an employer from overtime obligations. ACA: The 30-Hour Threshold and the 50-Employee Rule The ACA uses a different framework. Applicable Large Employers (ALEs)—generally employers with 50 or more full-time and full-time-equivalent employees—may be required to offer affordable health coverage to full-time employees or potentially pay a penalty. For ACA purposes, a full-time employee is generally one who averages at least 30 hours of service per week. Organizations below the ALE threshold are not subject to the ACA's Employer Shared Responsibility mandate, although they may still choose to offer health coverage to part-time employees. Special Case: Variable-Hour Employees Some employees do not have predictable schedules. For variable-hour employees, employers may use measurement methods that evaluate hours worked over a defined period to determine whether an employee should be treated as full-time. Employers should also understand the ACA full-time and variable-hour rules , which can affect how employee status is determined for benefits eligibility and compliance purposes. Accurate time tracking and documentation are especially important when managing variable-hour workforces. Handling HR and Compliance on Your Own? Answer a few quick questions to see which HR solution fits your business. Find My HR Solution State-Specific Rules: What to Know Beyond Federal Requirements Federal law is only part of the picture. States may impose additional requirements relating to wages, overtime, scheduling, and benefits. For example, while a part-time employee may not reach the 40 hours per week threshold to earn overtime under the FLSA, even a part-time employee could easily exceed the 8 hours per day threshold in California. For example, California has its own employment regulations and often operates under standards that differ from federal guidelines. Because employment laws vary significantly by jurisdiction, employers should review the requirements applicable to each state or locality in which employees work. For organizations with multi-state workforces, maintaining consistent policies while accounting for state- and local-specific obligations can be especially challenging. How to Set Your Part-Time and Full-Time Policy Because employers often have discretion in defining part-time and full-time status, a clear and documented policy is essential. Consider the following steps: 1. Establish Hours Thresholds Determine the number of hours employees must regularly work to qualify as full-time. Many employers use thresholds between 30 and 40 hours per week. Consider compliance requirements when setting the threshold. 2. Document the Policy Include expectations and eligibility criteria in your employee handbook and related HR documents. 3. Align Benefits Eligibility Define which benefits are available to part-time employees , full-time employees, or both. Ensure eligibility rules are applied consistently. 4. Communicate Expectations Clearly Employment offers , onboarding materials, and employee communications should clearly explain work schedules, part-time versus full-time status, and benefits eligibility. Consistent communication can help reduce misunderstandings and support compliance efforts. Benefits Eligibility: What Part-Time Employees May Receive Many employers assume part-time employees are not eligible for benefits, but that is not always the case. Some benefits may be required under law, while others are discretionary. Benefits Often Required by Law Depending on jurisdiction and circumstances, part-time employees are also eligible for: Workers' compensation coverage and Unemployment insurance protections, and may be eligible for other certain state-mandated benefits. Benefits Often Determined by Employer Policy Employers may choose whether to provide part-time employees: Health insurance (when not legally required) Paid time off (again, when not legally required) Retirement contributions or matching programs Wellness and employee assistance programs Organizations should carefully document eligibility requirements to ensure consistent administration. The SECURE Act Change: 401(k) Eligibility for Long-Term Part-Time Employees Under the SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022, many employers that sponsor 401(k) plans must allow certain long-term part-time employees to participate if they satisfy applicable service requirements. Generally, employees who are age 21 or older and work at least 500 hours in two consecutive 12-month periods may become eligible to make elective deferrals into the plan. Because these requirements continue to evolve, employers should work closely with plan administrators and advisors to understand how the rules affect their workforce. Switching Employees Between Part-Time and Full-Time Status Employee work schedules are not always permanent. Organizations may increase or reduce scheduled hours as business needs change. When doing so, employers should consider: Benefits eligibility start and end dates Health plan enrollment requirements Applicable waiting period rules Payroll and timekeeping updates Clear communication regarding status changes A documented process for moving employees between full-time and part-time can help ensure employees understand how a transition may affect compensation, schedules, and benefits. Special Cases: Interns and Seasonal Employees Some workforce categories require additional attention. Interns Employers should evaluate whether internship programs meet applicable wage-and-hour requirements and whether interns affect benefit eligibility determinations. Seasonal Employees Seasonal workers may be subject to special ACA measurement rules depending on the circumstances and duration of employment. Common Pitfalls Employers often encounter the same mistakes when establishing part-time policies. Assuming Federal Law Defines Part-Time - Many business leaders are surprised to learn that no universal federal definition exists. Failing to Document Policies - An unwritten policy can create inconsistent treatment and employee confusion. Overlooking State Requirements - State laws can introduce obligations beyond federal standards. Ignoring Retirement Plan Changes - Long-term part-time employees may have rights under current 401(k) eligibility rules that employers did not previously need to consider. Final Thoughts Defining part-time and full-time employment may seem like a straightforward policy decision, but it can have significant implications for benefits eligibility, overtime obligations, ACA requirements, retirement plans, and overall workforce management. As organizations grow and operate across multiple jurisdictions, maintaining consistent and compliant employment policies often becomes more complex. Establishing clear definitions, documenting policies, and regularly reviewing federal and state requirements can help employers support compliance efforts while creating a more consistent experience for employees. Frequently Asked Questions How many hours per week is part-time? There is no federal standard. Employers commonly classify employees working fewer than 30 to 35 hours per week as part-time, although internal policies vary. Do part-time employees get benefits? Sometimes. Eligibility depends on employer policy, applicable federal requirements, state laws, and the specific benefit involved. Do part-time employees receive overtime? Yes. If a non-exempt part-time employee works more than 40 hours in a workweek, federal overtime requirements apply. Overtime requirements apply after 8 hours in a day in California. Can I engage independent contractors instead of hiring part-time employees? Not simply as a way to avoid employment obligations. Worker classification must reflect the true nature of the relationship, and misclassification can create compliance and financial risks. How has the SECURE Act affected part-time employees? The SECURE Act and SECURE 2.0 expanded retirement plan participation opportunities for certain long-term part-time employees, making tracking hours more important than ever. title: How This Studio Became the Secret Weapon Behind Fortune 500 Gifting
summary: From her living room to Fortune 500 clients—how Telescope Studio is redefining corporate gifting through design and local makers.
body_text: You know the letdown of a bad swag bag—the branded stress ball, the pen that quits on day two, the tote you’ll never carry. Chloe Sapienza built Telescope Studio, the corporate gifting studio she co-founded with her husband, as the antidote to that. A graphic designer by training, Chloe treats gifting as a design problem: How do you turn a company’s values into an object people actually keep? Telescope answers that by sourcing from local makers and small brands—which makes it a genuine distribution channel for exactly the kind of early-stage founders who read Shopify Masters. Here, Chloe shares her method for choosing gifts that land, and a practical numbers-backed path for makers who want their products in the mix. On what separates a gift people keep from one that ends up in the trash: The difference comes down to not choosing out of fear. When you’re giving to a whole group, there’s this pull toward the universal thing—the item you’re sure everyone will want. But that safe choice is actually the hardest one to get right. It’s hard for people to solve, and honestly it’s hard for us to solve sometimes too. When a company comes to us, there are so many variables. There’s the budget, the existing brand guidelines, the timeline, everybody’s preferences, and this desire for everything to be uniformly liked. That’s what makes it fun for us, though—figuring out how to creatively problem solve within those parameters. That’s what makes any creative endeavor interesting. And a lot of the depth can come through who you’ve chosen to be the purveyor. It might still be a water bottle or a candle or a yoga mat, but the story you tell around it, the way you source it, the makers you work with—that’s what makes it land for people. Telescope Studio sources from local makers and small brands to bring intention to every corporate gift. Telescope Studio On using metaphor to turn a brand value into an object: There are different approaches, but one of the best ways to translate a brand or a philosophy into a product is to think in metaphor. You use it to pull out the elements of what’s being communicated through the branding, then translate that into the objects you’re sourcing. So say a company’s brand value is transparency. We might choose a water bottle that’s transparent, made out of glass—something that calls to action the value being presented. It’s an easy example, but that’s the idea. The object itself reinforces what the brand is trying to say. On the Hawaii offsite that proved local sourcing keeps gifts in people’s hands: We just did a company offsite for a team in Hawaii—600 employees—and we sourced everything from local makers on the island. They ran a survey after the event, and so many people talked about how meaningful it was, and how that was a reason they kept the products afterward. The items were genuinely useful during the event, but people loved that it connected to the local economy and to brands from the region we were celebrating. Those are kind of classic items on their own. It’s the story you tell around them and the makers you choose that make them things people actually want. Drawing more of this industry toward our local economy is one of our main goals. I have such a passion for product and product design, and I get a lot of joy out of knowing we’re helping bring those brands into the fold. There are big suppliers that source from overseas, and that’s what catapulted the industry to where it is—no negative feelings there. But I don’t think that’s where it’s going. More intention behind gifting is going to mean sourcing locally, and I think that’s what most people are looking for now. Telescope designs, warehouses, and ships every order from one downtown Los Angeles studio space. Telescope Studio On how a small maker gets on a distributor’s radar: We’re constantly doing research and reaching out to brands. We use marketplaces, we find people on Instagram, and brands reach out to us too. There’s a way on our website to contact us and get involved. Generally, the thing that matters is making sure you’re set up for wholesale and open to slightly larger orders. There are a lot of distributors in our industry who’d be interested in working with a small maker, so it’s really about finding the right ones to partner with. On the order sizes that make a small brand pitchable: Anywhere from about 25 units per item up to 2,500 is the general range. Some orders are much bigger, but for a smaller maker, even having 500 units of a certain colorway or SKU on hand makes you a much more appealing thing for us to pitch. We’re often throwing a bunch of ideas in front of a customer to figure out what they’ll get excited about, so there’s a lot of sourcing happening behind the scenes. Knowing a brand actually has the inventory matters. If a customer decides to buy and then it’s not available, that’s a problem. Every product Telescope pitches is chosen to reflect something specific about the client's brand values. Telescope Studio On treating corporate gifting as a distribution channel for your product: I talk about this with makers a lot: Gifting is another way wholesaling can become a real strategy for you. It gets your product into the hands of future qualified customers, and it does it in a really delightful setting, because they’re receiving it as a gift. It comes to them in a way that feels accessible. For a new product or a new brand, getting involved in gifting is a smart way to get yourself out there. On what a good gift is actually supposed to do: A really great gift has an outcome, and that outcome should be the intended purpose from the start. Sometimes it’s retention—employees feeling more supported and more a part of the team. Sometimes it’s recognition, or celebrating a milestone. For sales and marketing teams, it can lead to conversion or to a better relationship with a customer, because it feels personal. It’s not just an email. It’s a physical object that reminds you of that person, that company, that reason. If a gift doesn’t do that, it’s missed the mark. That’s the big misconception, too. Companies think they need lots of different things all the time. You don’t. It can just be one really thoughtful thing. Hear Chloe’s full conversation on Shopify Masters for more on why Telescope brought warehousing and fulfillment in-house, the tote bags that showed up handbag-sized, and the soccer career she walked away from at 20.

summary: Topline data from CHAPTER-3, a pivotal Phase 3 study of deucrictibant XR for the prophylaxis of HAE attacks, expected in 3Q2026 Deucrictibant IR NDA under review by the FDA with PDUFA date of April 23, 2027; MAA validated by the EMA in July 2026 Enrollment ongoing in CREAATE, a pivotal study of
body_text: Topline data from CHAPTER-3, a pivotal Phase 3 study of deucrictibant XR for the prophylaxis of HAE attacks, expected in 3Q2026 Deucrictibant IR NDA under review by the FDA with PDUFA date of April 23, 2027; MAA validated by the EMA in July 2026 Enrollment ongoing in CREAATE, a pivotal study of deucrictibant for the prophylactic and on-demand treatment of AAE-C1INH attacks Strong financial position with cash and cash equivalents of €318 million as of June 30, 2026 ZUG, Switzerland, Aug. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Pharvaris (Nasdaq: PHVS), a late-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel, oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonists to help address unmet needs of those living with bradykinin-mediated angioedema (AE-BK), such as hereditary angioedema (HAE) and acquired angioedema due to C1 inhibitor deficiency (AAE-C1INH), today announced financial results for the second quarter ending on June 30, 2026, and provided a business update. “Pharvaris continues to make strong progress advancing deucrictibant IR toward potential regulatory approval, moving closer to our goal of helping address unmet needs of people living with HAE by providing a therapy that can offer rapid and sustained attack relief and resolution with a single oral capsule. In parallel to our recent regulatory successes, our ongoing pre-commercial activities are designed to support a timely, successful U.S. launch,” said Berndt Modig, Chief Executive Officer of Pharvaris. “Announcing pivotal data from CHAPTER-3, expected this quarter, will mark another key milestone for Pharvaris as we develop deucrictibant for both the prevention and on-demand treatment of bradykinin-mediated angioedema attacks. The financing we completed in May extends our cash runway into 2028, enabling us to properly prepare for deucrictibant’s launch and consider lifecycle management opportunities while maintaining capital discipline.” Recent Business Updates Development Pipeline Topline data from CHAPTER-3 ( NCT06669754 ) expected in 3Q2026. CHAPTER-3 is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study of orally administered deucrictibant extended-release (XR) tablet for the prophylaxis against angioedema attacks in adults and adolescents (12 years and older) with HAE. Eighty-five participants were enrolled and randomized in a 2:1 ratio to receive deucrictibant XR (40 mg/day), the intended commercial formulation, or placebo, once daily for 24 weeks. Pharvaris expects to announce topline data from CHAPTER-3 in the third quarter of 2026. Enrollment in CHAPTER-4 ( NCT06679881 ) progressing as planned. CHAPTER-4 is a long-term, open-label extension study of orally administered deucrictibant XR (40 mg/day) for the prophylactic treatment of HAE attacks. The goal of the study is to evaluate the long-term safety and effectiveness of deucrictibant XR in the prophylactic treatment of HAE attacks. Review of marketing authorization applications of deucrictibant immediate-release (IR) capsule as a potential on-demand treatment of HAE attacks underway by regulatory authorities. In July 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) accepted to review the Company’s New Drug Application (NDA) for deucrictibant IR for the on-demand treatment of HAE attacks, with the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) action date set for April 23, 2027. In July 2026, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) validated the marketing authorization application (MAA) for deucrictibant IR and began its formal review of the MAA under the centralized procedure. Expanded Access Program (EAP) for deucrictibant IR for the on-demand treatment of HAE attacks opened in the U.S. EAPs are a potential pathway for people with a serious or immediately life-threatening disease or condition to gain access to an investigational medical product for treatment outside of clinical trials when no comparable or satisfactory alternative therapy options are available. The U.S. EAP for deucrictibant IR is available to people in U.S. living with HAE meeting eligibility requirements. Healthcare professionals interested in making requests for access to deucrictibant IR through the EAP can refer to https://mytomorrows.com/pharvaris/healthcareprofessional/ and/or email Pharvaris’ Medical Affairs at expandedaccess@pharvaris.com . Enrollment in CREAATE ( NCT07266805 ) progressing as planned. CREAATE is a global, pivotal Phase 3 study evaluating orally administered deucrictibant for the prophylactic and on-demand treatment of AAE-C1INH attacks. Assessment of AAE-C1INH disease burden and validation of clinical trial endpoints published in Frontiers in Immunology . Qualitative interviews provided evidence of the impact of AAE-C1INH on participants’ lives and overall well-being, and the study findings informed the clinical outcome assessment strategy for CREAATE, the first phase 3 clinical trial specifically studying AAE-C1INH. Evidence supporting bradykinin B2 receptor as a validated therapeutic target in bradykinin-mediated angioedema published in Clinical Reviews in Allergy & Immunology . This summary of the growing body of evidence explores the critical role of bradykinin B2 receptor in the pathogenesis of bradykinin-mediated angioedema and supports bradykinin B2 receptor antagonism as a therapeutic strategy for bradykinin-mediated diseases, including HAE and AAE-C1INH, as well as, potentially, other allergic and immunological conditions. Corporate Peng Lu, M.D., Ph.D., promoted to newly created role of President. Leveraging the company’s scientific rigor and reflecting the depth of Dr. Lu’s contributions, Pharvaris has brought its research, development, and commercial functions under one leadership structure by promoting Dr. Lu to President, effective June 2026, strengthening Pharvaris’ ability to deliver on its strategic priorities. Closed $132 million underwritten offering. The proceeds from the offering of $132.3 million of shares extends cash runway into 2028. Note on International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Pharvaris is a Foreign Private Issuer and prepares and reports consolidated financial statements and financial information in accordance with IFRS as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board. Pharvaris maintains its books and records in the Euro currency. About Deucrictibant Deucrictibant is a novel, potent, orally bioavailable small-molecule bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist currently in clinical development. Deucrictibant is being investigated for its potential to prevent the occurrence of bradykinin-mediated angioedema attacks and to treat the manifestations of attacks if/when they occur by inhibiting bradykinin signaling through the bradykinin B2 receptor. Pharvaris is developing two formulations of deucrictibant for oral administration: an extended-release tablet to enable sustained absorption and efficacy as prophylactic treatment, and an immediate-release capsule to enable rapid onset of activity for on-demand treatment. Deucrictibant has been granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of bradykinin-mediated angioedema by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, the European Commission, and Swissmedic. About Pharvaris Pharvaris is a late-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel, oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonists to help address unmet needs in bradykinin-mediated conditions, including all types of bradykinin-mediated angioedema. Pharvaris’ aspiration is to offer therapies with injectable-like efficacy™, a well-tolerated profile, and the convenience of oral administration to prevent and treat bradykinin-mediated angioedema attacks. By delivering on this aspiration, Pharvaris aims to provide a new standard of care in bradykinin-mediated angioedema. For more information, visit https://pharvaris.com/ .
